title: Quietly Braised Filipino Pork Stew
description: A pungent and chewy Filipino dish featuring sake-cooked pork, perfect for a date night, and a shojin-friendly option for those seeking a meat-based meal with a focus on simplicity and restraint, served in a traditional Korean brass bowl.
instructions: Heat the sake in a large Korean brass bowl over medium heat until it starts to simmer.
Add the pork pieces to the bowl and cook until browned on all sides.
Add the soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, star anise, and black pepper to the bowl and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 2 hours.
Remove the bowl from the heat and let it rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with sliced green onions and steamed rice on the side.
Let the stew rest for 10 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
Serve the stew in the Korean brass bowl, garnished with additional sliced green onions if desired.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F, then rest 3 minutes before serving.
